results.summary: This design is an analog chiral exceptional-point sensor built around two nominally matched on-chip LC tanks at ~2.7 GHz. It uses unidirectional coupling through an NMOS source follower and a coupling MIM cap to place the system on an exceptional-point line. A small capacitive perturbation on the V1 tank produces a frequency splitting in the V2 spectrum that scales as the square root of the perturbation. Testing requires a vector network analyzer reaching at least 3 GHz and a Tiny Tapeout breakout board with u.fl connectors.

results.summary: This project is a UART responder that listens for the ASCII string 'MARCO' and replies with '\n\rPOLO!\n\r' after a 10 microsecond delay. It also drives a single WS2812b LED that blips from red to green upon detection. The design is implemented in Verilog and includes debug outputs for baud ticks and UART status. Silicon testing confirmed the UART reply but the LED behavior was not observed.
